ModInfo.description:
[h1]Choose your ruler's first strength instead of rolling it.[/h1]
With [b]Leader = Pick Later[/b] and [b]Customize Leader off[/b], your ruler no longer starts with a random strength trait. On [b]turn 2[/b] you get the familiar Promote popup and pick one yourself.
Your archetype choice and your ratings are untouched.
[h1]What you get[/h1] [list] [*][b]Turn 1[/b] — you found your capital and pick your archetype. An event, [i]The Measure of a King[/i] (or Queen), tells you the choice is coming. [*][b]Turn 2[/b] — the Promote popup offers [b]four traits[/b] and no rating options. [/list]
[b]Leader with no job[/b] — four picks from the full pool of 33 strengths. [b]Leader already a general[/b] — three general strengths (from the pool of 15) and one governor strength, just like a level up. [b]Leader already a governor[/b] — three governor strengths (from the pool of 18) and one general strength, just like a level up.
[h1]The pools[/h1] [b]General (15)[/b] — traits that improve the unit your leader commands: [list] [*]Besieger, Bloodthirsty, Brave, Engineer, Fierce, Heckler, Herbalist, Highlander, Horsebane, Ranger, Shieldbearer, Steadfast, Swift, Tough, Tracker [/list]
[b]Governor (18)[/b] — traits that improve the city your leader governs: [list] [*]Affable, Carpenter, Cultivator, Cunning, Delver, Eloquent, Equestrian, Frugal, Inspiring, Intelligent, Naturalist, Pathfinder, Prosperous, Righteous, Robust, Strict, Vigilant, Warlike [/list]
The two do not overlap, so a general's fourth option is always a governor strength, and a governor's fourth is always a general one.
[h1]Multiplayer[/h1] Depending on the leader (unassigned, governor, general), players will get a choice of four traits from the appropriate pool. These four traits are the same for both players if they're in the same pool.
For example, if both players assign their leader as governor on turn 1, they'll both pick from four traits (3 of which are from the gov pool, 1 from the general pool). The four traits offered will be the same for both players.
Another example: If one player assigns their leader as a general and the other leaves their leader unassigned, the first player will pick from four traits (3 from the general pool, 1 from the governor pool). The second player will pick from four traits (4 from the overall pool of strengths). These will not be the same four traits.
[h1]Notes[/h1] [list] [*]Everyone in a multiplayer game needs the mod enabled. [*]Players using a fixed archetype, a preset leader, or the leader customizer are unaffected. [*]No base game files are changed. Built and tested against 1.0.84365. [/list]
[b]Source:[/b] https://github.com/alcaras/OldWorld-Turn2StartingTrait
